rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this candidate escalates obfuscation from a conservative baseline: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain because flops-6 is dominated by floating-point arithmetic where instruction substitution obscures the numeric kernels cheaply and safely, and IBR/ICALL are raised next since indirect branching and calls add control-flow indirection with moderate cost on a tiny 791-byte text section where size blowup is affordable. FLA and BCF are kept at moderately high security weights but with the largest RuntimeCost/SizeCost penalties (0.5-0.55) because this benchmark is a tight FP loop where flattening and bogus control flow multiply loop-body overhead; the moderate penalties let the feature-driven selector apply them where per-function features justify it rather than globally. SPLIT is cheap and useful for structural diversity. IGV carries the highest CorrectnessRisk (0.3) since global variable indirection interacts poorly with optimized FP code, but remains enabled with a solid security weight given the successful prior build. Overall the table biases toward strong transformation while penalizing only the two highest-overhead passes, balancing reverse-engineering resistance against runtime on a hot numeric loop.
